title: Ike's Morning Digest
data_note: Built from publisher RSS metadata (titles + teaser text). `coverage_window_hours` is the default (40h); several feeds use a longer `rollingHours` (see `scripts/build-digest.mjs`) so rows align with what is still on each publisher’s listing pages. Commercial Observer keeps its retail category + hub supplement; TRD adds a New York–filtered global retail tag feed. PincusCo uses the live site feed only (`/category/retail/feed/` is stale). **CRE Daily** retail briefs come from `credaily.com/sectors/retail/feed/`. **WSJ** is the Dow Jones real-estate feed with lifestyle and opinion dropped. **The New York Times** keeps real-estate and property stories only. **Traded** is commercial deal briefs from its news listing. Open each link for the full article (subscriptions may apply in the browser).

section_overviews.commercial_observer:
Italian Kitchen Manufacturer Officine Gullo to Open Store at 95 Madison Avenue: Hey now, hey now , these kitchens are what dreams are made of. Italy’s Officine Gullo , a manufacturer of luxury commercial and residential kitchens, has taken 3,200 square feet of ground-floor retail space at Sunlight Development ’s 95 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned.

Got Your Six Cannabis Dispensary Secures Manhattan Flagship: A cannabis store is opening its Manhattan flagship location at the base of a luxury Tribeca condominium building. Got Your Six , a licensed dispensary based in New Jersey, has signed a 2,300-square-foot lease at 256 West Street , also known as 92 Laight Street .

NBA Store Seeks New, Larger Location Up to 25K Square Feet: Jump ball. The NBA Store, which is operated by Fanatics -owned sports apparel company Lids , is planning to relocate from its longtime retail location at 545 Fifth Avenue into a larger space, Commercial Observer can first report.

Carnegie Diner & Cafe Operator to Open New Restaurant at 7 Penn Plaza: Carnegie Hospitality is opening its next Carnegie Diner & Cafe in Manhattan’s Penn District. The restaurateur signed on the dotted line last month to take over fast-casual chain Smashburger ’s lease at the Feil Organization ’s 7 Penn Plaza , Commercial Observer has learned.
section_overviews.cre_daily:
Institutions Turn to JVs for Grocery-Anchored Retail: Institutional investors are using joint ventures to gain exposure to retail, especially grocery-anchored centers, citing supply-and-demand fundamentals and long-term income growth.

Grocery-Anchored Retail Premium Hinges on Store and Lease: Grocery-anchored retail is among the most competitive investment niches, with 2025 transaction volume near $11B and cap rates averaging 6.7%, but the grocery label alone doesn’t justify a premium.

Younger Partners Buys 261K SF Terrell Power Center: Younger Partners Investments bought Crossroads at Terrell, a fully leased 260,876 SF power center 30 miles east of Dallas, from RealtyLink for an undisclosed price. A regional bank’s senior loan and preferred equity from a national REIT financed the deal, and the center ranked as Texas’ third most-visited retail.

Banks Lock Up Manhattan Retail Space as Availability Hits Low: Bank of America took 16,000 square feet at 19 Union Square West and Citibank took 14,000 square feet at 170 West 72nd Street, two of Manhattan’s largest third-quarter retail leases.
section_overviews.new_york_post:
One of NYC’s final Gilded Age buildings sells for $42M — but is set for heartbreaking demolition: The 1891 Schieffelin-Bowne House marks a key milestone in Sedesco's yearslong Midtown assemblage, with plans for a 1,100-foot luxury tower taking shape.

California voters approve $11.25B housing bond, saddling state with decades of new debt: Written by state lawmakers, the measure aims to provide up to 40,000 multifamily rental units and assist another 40,000 households in buying a home.

Oakland Coliseum operator axes 1,600 workers as historic stadium sale goes down: The operator of the storied Oakland Coliseum and Oakland Arena is laying off workers en masse as Oakland officials prepare to sell both venues.

items.headline: Institutions Turn to JVs for Grocery-Anchored Retail
items.summary: Institutional investors are using joint ventures to gain exposure to retail, especially grocery-anchored centers, citing supply-and-demand fundamentals and long-term income growth. Investors want experienced operators with leasing, tenant-mix and local-market know-how, while operators get capital in return for acquisitions, development and redevelopment. JV equity is still hard to raise amid high rates, valuation uncertainty and buyer-seller gaps, so some investors are buying stakes in operating companies instead.…

items.headline: Grocery-Anchored Retail Premium Hinges on Store and Lease
items.summary: Grocery-anchored retail is among the most competitive investment niches, with 2025 transaction volume near $11B and cap rates averaging 6.7%, but the grocery label alone doesn’t justify a premium. Buyers should study store sales, the grocer’s competitive position and remodel plans, plus lease terms such as sales-based termination rights, co-tenancy clauses and replacement restrictions.…

items.headline: Got Your Six Cannabis Dispensary Secures Manhattan Flagship
items.summary: A cannabis store is opening its Manhattan flagship location at the base of a luxury Tribeca condominium building. Got Your Six , a licensed dispensary based in New Jersey, has signed a 2,300-square-foot lease at 256 West Street , also known as 92 Laight Street . The corner retail lease between Laight and Vestry streets occupies part of the ground floor at Riverloft Condominiums , a 13-story luxury complex, and is near Hudson River Park . Crain’s New York first reported on the deal.…

In September, financial services platform Intuit , the company behind programs including TurboTax , QuickBooks , Credit Karma and Mailchimp , signed a 3,546-square-foot lease at the 70-story property at 42-06 Orchard Street in Queens’ Long Island City neighborhood.…

items.headline: Banks Lock Up Manhattan Retail Space as Availability Hits Low
items.summary: Bank of America took 16,000 square feet at 19 Union Square West and Citibank took 14,000 square feet at 170 West 72nd Street, two of Manhattan’s largest third-quarter retail leases. Most bank activity is renewals and strategic relocations by existing tenants, and banks are returning to corner locations in a market where space is hard to replace. Prime corridor availability fell to a record-low 157 spaces, and one JLL broker has five or six more bank deals in progress, a sign of broader retail strength.…

items.headline: Hudson Valley Boutique Shop Signs Lease in Manhattan’s Nolita
items.summary: A Beacon, N.Y., knickknack shop is making its New York City debut with a store in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. Solstad House General Store signed a five-year, 1,200-square-foot lease at Emmanuel Stark ’s 167 Mott Street , with an asking rent of $6,750 per month, according to broker Meridian Retail Leasing .…

items.headline: CVS Split Would Create Two Public Companies by 2028
items.summary: CVS Health plans to separate into a healthcare solutions company and a retail pharmacy company, with the split expected to finish in the first half of 2028. The healthcare company keeps the CVS Health name and brands including Aetna and Caremark, while CVS Pharmacy will operate roughly 9,000 stores, MinuteClinic and mail pharmacy. A standalone 9,000-store retail tenant matters to net lease owners, though the announcement coverage gives no detail on how leases or guarantees will be handled.…

items.headline: Retail Net Absorption Hits 9.6M SF in Q3
items.summary: U.S. retail net absorption reached 9.6 million SF in Q3, the fifth consecutive positive quarter, led by neighborhood, community and strip centers at 2.4 million SF. Completions hit a quarterly low of 5.5 million SF and a record-low four-quarter total of 7.4 million SF, keeping availability at 4.8% and lifting asking rents 2.5%. Leasing is strong but investment volume fell 6% to $16.8 billion, so landlords hold pricing power while buyers stay cautious on asset-level pricing. Key Takeaways U.S.…

items.headline: Sports Clothing Brand RBX Direct Signs 5K-SF Garment District Lease
items.summary: An activewear brand has signed a lease for an office and showroom in Manhattan’s Garment District. RBX Direct took 4,800 square feet at Lal Sani ’s 102 West 38th Street , where asking rent was $35 per square foot, according to landlord broker Adams & Company . Adams & Company did not disclose the length of the lease or the name of the landlord, but the most recent filings in property records show the building has not traded hands since 1994 when it was purchased by Sani.…

items.headline: Life Time Inks 20-Year Lease at Crescent Heights’ Miami Dev Site
items.summary: Health club chain Life Time is coming to Miami’s Edgewater neighborhood. The high-end gym operator, formerly known as Life Time Fitness, signed a 20-year lease at 3180 Biscayne Boulevard , a 2.6-acre, full-block development site owned by Crescent Heights , according to documents filed to Miami-Dade County. The gym will likely be part of a mixed-use development using the Live Local Act , a Florida law that grants developers faster approvals if at least 40 percent of units are priced as workforce housing.…

items.headline: Amazon’s Same-Day Delivery Expansion Reignites Demand for Last-Mile Logistics
items.summary: When Amazon makes moves in the delivery business, the entire retail industry tends to reorient itself around the e-commerce giant. So, when a September report from Business Insider revealed preliminary plans for Amazon to embark on a “ massive blitz in same-day delivery ” with a proposed expansion of facilities code-named Project Mercury, industrial real estate took notice.…

items.headline: Apparel Brand American Giant Leases Brooklyn Store at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue
items.summary: San Francisco-based apparel brand American Giant has arrived in Brooklyn. The manufacturer of sportswear and casual clothing made exclusively in the United States has signed a lease for 3,400 square feet at 83-85 Metropolitan Avenue in North Williamsburg, where it will open its first Brooklyn store, according to a source familiar with the deal.…

items.headline: Day Care Operator Inks 21K-SF Lease in Brooklyn’s Gravesend
items.summary: A new Ukrainian day care, Ukrainian New Generation Kids Daycare , has signed a 21,000-square-foot lease at Yakov Ostrovsky ‘s 1940 Shore Parkway in Gravesend, Brooklyn. The day care center is expected to open in the entirety of the four-story commercial building in the second quarter of 2027, and will be able to accommodate 300 children, according to Ripco Real Estate , which represented both the landlord and the tenant in this deal. The length of the lease was not disclosed.…

items.headline: For Mall Giant Macerich, More Turnaround in Q3
items.summary: Mall owner Macerich ’s net operating income (NOI) and revenue were up annually in the third quarter of 2026 behind strong leasing and generally favorable conditions for owners of top-shelf brick-and-mortar retail. The Santa Monica, Calif.-based real estate investment trust (REIT), however, recorded a loss attributable to the company of more than $16.73 million for the quarter.…
